feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon to share a stage to promote curbs on AI
entry.summary: The poles of U.S. politics are coming together over AI. Sanders and Bannon will appear at the "Pro-Human Assembly" in Washington, D.C., to convince Congress to work faster to curb the impact of AI.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: President Trump downplays fears about AI risks, Supreme Court rejects Trump's efforts to enact mail-in voting restrictions for the midterms, Kennedy Center says it's on the brink of bankruptcy.

entry.title: Supreme Court refuses to allow Trump's mail voting restrictions for the midterms
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected President Trump's push for new mail-in voting restrictions for the midterm election.

entry.title: Attorney discusses the Kennedy Center's financial woes and Trump's naming efforts
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez talks to Attorney Greg Werkheiser, of the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, about Trump's efforts to add his name to the Kennedy Center and the financial trouble it's facing.

entry.title: Ex-CIA chief issued subpoena in Trump 'grand conspiracy' investigation, lawyer says
entry.summary: John Brennan has been subpoenaed to testify before a Florida grand jury in a Justice Department probe into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against President Trump.

entry.title: The Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail voting restrictions for this year's midterms
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected the Trump administration's request to allow mail-in voting restrictions under a U.S. Postal Service plan for the midterm general election.

entry.title: Trump's EPA repeals pollution limits on fossil fuel power plants
entry.summary: The Trump administration is eliminating limits on climate-warming pollution from the nation's fossil fuel power plants. Environmental groups say this will impact the climate and public health.

entry.title: This city led the way on reparations for Black people. Trump is trying to stop it
entry.summary: Evanston, Ill., became the first U.S. city to compensate Black people for historical discrimination. The Justice Department is trying to kill its program before other cities follow suit.

entry.title: Forecast says families will spend more to heat their homes this winter
entry.summary: It's probably going to cost more to heat your home this winter. Forecasters say heating bills are likely to climb faster than overall inflation, despite what's expected to be a relatively mild winter.

entry.title: Kennedy Center board says venue could close soon due to financial woes
entry.summary: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Washington Post arts and government reporter Jonathan Edwards about internal documents showing the Kennedy Center could close as soon as Tuesday.
